english.synthetic: Written for tests. No real patient, no real person.

segments.text: Good day, Mrs. Georgescu. I see you came with your daughter.
Good day, Doctor. Yes, Ana brought me, because I don't remember everything I need anymore.
Good day. Mom lost her diabetes tablets again last week and her blood sugar was high.
How high was it?
In the morning 210, in the evening 180. I measured it with her device.
Mrs. Georgescu, what tablets are you taking now?
Metformin, I think 1000, in the morning and evening. But sometimes I forget the evening one.
And how is the left foot? Last time you had a small wound on the heel.
It still hurts and turns red in the evening.
Let me check. The wound hasn't closed and the skin around it is red. You need to see a surgeon.
Where do we go?
I will refer you to surgery, to the outpatient clinic of the county hospital. Try to get an appointment during the next week.
I will take care of the appointment, I'll call tomorrow morning.
Very well. Until then, daily dressing with physiological serum and betadine. The community assistant can come to your home to show you how to do it.
That would be a great help, I work until 5.
I will inform the community assistant, Mrs. Ioana, to visit you on Monday afternoon.
And what about the tablets, since I keep forgetting them?
I recommend a box of pills for the days of the week. Ana, please prepare it for the whole week on Sunday evening.
Sure, I'll buy it from the pharmacy today.
I also want a hemoglobin A1c and a urine test. Do those at the lab by Friday.
We'll do them on Thursday, since I'm free.
Come back then on November 20th at 11, with the results and with the medical letter from the surgeon.
November 20th, at 11. Ana, please write it down, please.
I noted it. Thank you very much, Doctor.
You're welcome. If fever appears or the foot swells, come immediately.
